Avery —

Thanks for taking our questionnaire. We received the FEN-2192 KMS/HSM section back from the security review board and have a few clarifications before we proceed to the procurement checklist. Attached is the spreadsheet with line-item questions (see tab: TLS & Key Ops).

Key points where we need explicit confirmation and evidence:
- BYOK import: do you support wrapped-key import (RSA-OAEP / AES wrap) and can we bring RSA/ECC wrapping keys from our on-prem HSM? What formats are supported (PKCS#8, PKCS#12, KMIP import)?
- HSM attestation: do you publish HSM vendor & firmware details and provide attestation artifacts (certificate chains or signed attestation)? Is the HSM FIPS 140-2/3 validated, and can you supply the report we can include in our vendor risk register?
- Key rotation / rollbacks: expected maximum RTO for a customer-requested rotation rollback and whether cache invalidation is supported across replicas in a multi-region deployment.
- TLS binding & mTLS: if we require mutual TLS between our frontends and your private deployment, can we supply our own root CA and have you pin client certs at the load balancer / ingress?
- Backup & escrow: describe the secure key escrow or recovery process for disaster scenarios and any geographic restrictions.

Please respond with short answers and attach the evidence you can share under NDA. We're trying to close the security gate this week; a reply by EOD Wednesday (19 May) would be ideal.

Julia —

Thanks for the clear list. We can cover everything you requested; below is a concise summary and we will follow up with a short packet of artifacts (PDFs + diagrams). If useful, we can set a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow morning.

High-level answers (summary):
- BYOK import: supported. We accept wrapped master keys via RSA-OAEP or AES-KW; supported formats include PKCS#8 and PKCS#12 for wrapped exports, and KMIP 2.0 via our KMIP gateway for large-scale migrations. We provide a one-time import token + signed import transcript.
- HSM attestation: our HSM fleet runs vendor-certified modules (YubiHSM / Thales/Entrust depending on region) with published firmware and validation numbers. We can provide FIPS 140-2/3 module IDs and redacted attestation bundles under NDA.
- Key rotation & rollback: primary (root/master) key rotations are handled quarterly by default; data keys rotate per-customer policy (configurable; typical window 30 days). Rollbacks are supported only with explicit export and rewrap procedures; soft rollback across caches is 1–5 minutes for KV cache invalidation in normal operation, full global propagation depends on deployment topology.
- TLS binding / mTLS: we support customer-supplied CAs for mTLS on Private deployments; cert pinning at ingress is available for dedicated/private modes. Hosted customers can use our managed mTLS offering with customer-provided certs.
- Backup & escrow: disaster recovery uses an encrypted escrow mechanism with optional multi-party escrow & PKCS#11-protected export; geographic storage can be restricted to specified regions on request.

We will attach: Redwood_KMS_TLS_Response_20270517.pdf (detailed Q&A), HSM_Attestation_Summary_20270228.pdf (attestation metadata), and an import workflow image. Let me know if you want an evidence-only bundle (we can redact PII).

Avery

Julia —

Appended below are the formal answers and the artifacts we can share now. We've also uploaded a short evidence bundle to the secure link (see HubSpot). If anything needs more detail we can schedule a short call.

--- Formal responses (short) ---
1) BYOK import:
- Supported import modes: wrapped-key import via RSA-OAEP and AES-KW; accepted formats: PKCS#8 (wrapped), PKCS#12 (wrapped), and KMIP 2.0 via our KMIP gateway.
- Process: customer generates an asymmetric wrapping key in their HSM -> requests a one-time import token from Redwood -> wraps the master key -> uploads the wrapped blob. We return a signed import manifest for audit.
- Evidence provided: Import_Process_Workflow.png (workflow), Redwood_KMS_TLS_Response_20270517.pdf (detailed steps).

2) HSM attestation & FIPS status:
- HSMs: Thales Luna SA (US pool) and Yubico/Entrust modules in other regions. We publish module vendor & firmware IDs and can provide redacted attestation bundles under NDA.
- Validation: FIPS 140-2/3 module IDs included in HSM_Attestation_Summary_20270228.pdf (redacted).

3) Key rotation & rollback:
- Default rotation cadence: root/master keys: quarterly; data keys: configurable, default 30 days.
- Cache invalidation & RTO: soft invalidation within the same region typically <= 5 minutes. Cross-region propagation targeted <= 30 minutes; exact times depend on your deployed topology.
- Rollback: supported as an extraordinary operation requiring explicit export/rewrap and coordination with our ops team; timing and SLA are covered by Dedicated/Private contracts.

4) TLS binding & mTLS:
- Private & Dedicated deployments: customer-supplied root CA and mTLS client cert pinning supported at ingress/load-balancer level. Hosted customers: managed mTLS available; you can bring certs or use our managed CA.
- We support certificate rotation workflows and certificate revocation list (CRL)/OCSP checks at the edge.

5) Backup & escrow / geographic checks:
- Escrow: encrypted, PKCS#11-backed escrow available; multi-party escrow possible on request. Storage region restrictions can be enforced contractually.

- Import_Process_Workflow.png (process diagram)
